meta.note: Educational comparison, not a prediction and not an official evacuation plan. Synthetic households, illustrative fires. "People still there when embers arrived" and "still home when the fire front arrived" count synthetic people at that moment; they are not casualty counts. Costs are screening ranges copied from earlier outputs (null = not priced, never zero).
meta.baseline: DEFAULT_PLAN (js/sim.js), Time Study case S6 (fall night) for every fire
meta.holdsRule: better in every same-seed pair (15 of 15), SOURCE_NOTES P19

ember.label: People still there when embers arrived
ember.def: synthetic people at home, on the road or without a car when embers reached their street, including people in zones never told to leave (the Simple-view headline; js/presets.js)

front.label: People still home when the fire front arrived
front.def: synthetic people still at home when the fire front reached their street (summary().fireFrontHome); early leavers and bought-out households never count

cutOff.label: Cars cut off by fire
cutOff.def: vehicles on the road at the end of the run with no route to safety (summary().vehiclesNoRoute; the results panel's "vehicles cut off by fire")

engine.label: Hill residents an engine cannot reach within 5 minutes
engine.def: synthetic Berkeley Fire Zones 2–3 residents whose street no engine reaches from a station within the City's 5-minute standard, at ignition, under the run's parked cars (summary().engineReachBeyond5People); the same on every fire for a seed

clear90.label: 90% clearance (min)
clear90.def: minutes from the first order until 90% of vehicles starting in Order zones have left the order area (summary().clearP90, the Time Study's ETE); null if never reached in the run, which counts as slower than any finished run

levers.title: Control: baseline rerun, no change
levers.what: DEFAULT_PLAN again; must match the baseline exactly

levers.title: Leave early on a Red Flag day
levers.what: half of hill households (Fire Zones 2–3) leave on the Red Flag warning, before any fire starts

cost.note: Little capital cost: a warning and outreach the City already runs. The real costs are households' time away from home on every Red Flag day, unpriced.

levers.cannotMeasure: Whether half of hill households would actually leave on a real Red Flag day, and whether they keep doing it after Red Flag days with no fire (warning fatigue). The simulator places the early leavers out of the area before ignition.

levers.title: Decide faster
levers.what: first evacuation order 5 minutes after the fire starts instead of 10, as in today's plan
levers.how: js/presets.js orderSooner Plan B delta (the preset compares 20 → 5 min; here the baseline is DEFAULT_PLAN's 10)

cost.note: Little capital cost: staffing and authority to issue an order on first report. Orders that turn out to be unnecessary have a social cost, unpriced.

levers.cannotMeasure: Whether a fire can be confirmed and an order issued 5 minutes after ignition, and the cost of orders for fires that would have been caught. How fast alerts reach people is not modeled separately.

levers.title: One-side parking on narrow hill streets
levers.what: parking on one side only in Fire Zones 2–3

cost.note: Little capital cost (signs and paint), plus enforcement and lost parking for hill residents; not priced in this project.

levers.cannotMeasure: Enforcement on every hill street, night after night, and where the displaced cars go (driveways, other streets). Engines only drive in this simulator, so better engine access does not change the fire or who is still there.

levers.title: Red curb on the lowest block of Panoramic Way
levers.what: no parking on the 49 m lowest block of Panoramic Way only
levers.how: tools/widening-core.mjs noParkingEdge on widening pinch WP-001 (edge 992, retreat.json engineFoot)

cost.note: Paint and signs for 49 m of curb at $1–$4 per foot (assumption, unsourced; SOURCE_NOTES WD5); 7 parking spaces lost.

levers.cannotMeasure: Enforcement, and where the 7 cars that park there today go instead (probably farther up the same street). Engine access is its only effect here; engines do not fight the fire in this simulator.

levers.title: New link: City concept, Dwight Way to Dwight Place
levers.what: the City's "2nd Route Out" concept for Panoramic Hill

cost.note: Screening range: construction (FDOT flat-terrain figure to 3× for hillside) and acquisition; excludes relocation, engineering, environmental review and legal costs.

levers.cannotMeasure: Environmental review, slope and land acquisition, and whether the link is itself in the fire's path on the day. Costs exclude engineering, environmental review and legal costs (egress-candidates.json meta.cost.note).

link.street: Buena Vista Wy → W Parnassus Ct

cost.note: Screening range: construction (FDOT flat-terrain figure to 3× for hillside) and acquisition; excludes relocation, engineering, environmental review and legal costs.

levers.title: Widen the lowest block of Panoramic Way to 20 ft clear
levers.what: the 49 m lowest block widened to 20 ft clear between parked cars (the fire-code width), parking kept where it is today

cost.source: data/model/widening.json pinches WP-001 widening.fireCode (leastTaking and symmetric layouts)
cost.note: Screening range: construction and acquisition, low end of the least-taking layout to high end of the symmetric layout; not engineering or appraisal.

levers.cannotMeasure: Takings, retaining walls and construction on a steep street, and whether residents would park on the new pavement (the run posts parking to today's sides). Engines do not fight the fire in this simulator.

cost.source: data/model/widening.json pinches WP-007 widening.fireCode (leastTaking and symmetric layouts)
cost.note: Screening range: construction and acquisition, low end of the least-taking layout to high end of the symmetric layout; not engineering or appraisal.

levers.cannotMeasure: Takings, retaining walls and construction on a steep street, and whether residents would park on the new pavement (the run posts parking to today's sides). Engines do not fight the fire in this simulator.

levers.title: Buy out the lowest block of Panoramic Way, curb cleared
levers.what: the households on the lowest block of Panoramic Way bought out, and its parked cars gone
levers.how: world.retreat { edges: retreat.json engineFoot.edges, clearParking: true }, the engine-reach sensitivity of tools/retreat-sim.mjs

cost.note: Screening range: acquisition at block-group median home values, relocation under the URA, demolition; not an appraisal or a buyout proposal.

levers.cannotMeasure: Willingness to sell, the loss of homes and community, where displaced households go, and what happens to the vacated land. Removed households simply make no trip, so part of any drop is the bought-out people no longer being counted.

levers.title: R0: no added units in hill areas
levers.notComparable: R0 acts only under a future-growth scenario; on today's population (no growth) it changes nothing, so it is not comparable with these levers. Its results are in SOURCE_NOTES R1–R8 (with maximum growth, R0 lowers people still there when embers arrived in all 30 pairs).

levers.title: Contraflow on the main hill exit streets, officer-staffed
levers.what: both lanes outbound on the main hill exit streets wide enough between parked cars, started by officers at every entry point (default pool and arrival delay)
levers.how: plan { contraflow: main, contraflowMode: officers } (js/operations.js, SOURCE_NOTES CF1–CF16)

cost.note: Little capital cost; the cost is officers taken from other work (the shared pool), unpriced.

levers.cannotMeasure: Whether officers can reach and hold every entry point while the fire moves, drivers who ignore the closure, and the engines that can no longer drive up these streets beyond what engine reach shows.

levers.title: Contraflow on the main hill exit streets, pre-installed signs (battery backup)
levers.what: the same streets, started by rehearsed electronic signs and gates with battery backup
levers.how: plan { contraflow: main, contraflowMode: signs, contraflowPower: battery } (js/operations.js)

cost.note: Signs at every entry point; the run logs the count and a range per run (1923 fire, central, seed 1: 75 locations, about $1.1M–$4.3M; gates not costed). Not copied into this table because the count depends on the run.

levers.cannotMeasure: Whether drivers obey a sign without an officer, signs damaged by the fire itself, and rehearsal: the simulator assumes everyone follows the reversed lanes once they start.

levers.title: Police control of the pre-timed signals
levers.what: officers take over the City's 44 pre-timed signals on evacuation routes after their arrival delay (default pool)
levers.how: plan { police: pretimed } (js/operations.js, SOURCE_NOTES CF7, CF8, CF16)

cost.note: Little capital cost; officers taken from other work, unpriced.

levers.cannotMeasure: How officers actually direct traffic (the simulator gives a fixed capacity gain and outbound priority), radio coordination, and officers lost to other emergencies.

levers.title: Power shutoff
levers.notComparable: A hazard condition (scenario setting), not a mitigation: signals go dark and run as all-way stops. Its effect on the baseline and on contraflow is in SOURCE_NOTES CF14

levers.title: Constrained egress guidance (hypothetical pilot), all drivers follow
levers.what: drivers get a route only if it is no riskier than their own and at most a minute slower, or safer; nobody is told to wait
levers.how: plan { routing: guided, compliance: 1 } (js/guidance.js, SOURCE_NOTES DG1–DG30)

cost.note: Little capital cost in this table; a real system (data feeds, phones, liability) is unpriced.

levers.cannotMeasure: Today's plan already gives every driver an idealized, well-informed route, so guidance has little to add here; against drivers who follow habit it does better in every run (SOURCE_NOTES DG30). Phone networks failing, distrust, and the households a real system would leave worse off are not shown here.
